q-1788.name: Question 1
q-1788.problem: Suppose there are $7$ people who enter a race. Assuming there are no ties, in how many ways can the gold, silver, and bronze medals be awarded?
q-1788.worked_solution:
The number of permutations of $n$ objects taken $r$ at a time is given by the formula

$$
{}_{n}{P}_{r}=\frac{n!}{(n-r)!}.
$$

There are $7$ people, so $n=7.$ We want to select $3$ of those people for gold, silver and bronze, so we have $r=3.$ 

Therefore, the number of different ways to award the medals is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{}_{7}{P}_{3} & =\frac{7!}{(7-3)!} \\  & =\frac{7!}{4!} \\  & =\frac{7\cdot 6\cdot 5\cdot \cancel{4!}}{\cancel{4!}} \\  & =7\cdot 6\cdot 5 \\  & =210.\end{aligned}
$$

q-84983.name: Question 2
q-84983.problem: A bag contains $9$ different colored marbles. Jamie takes $4$ marbles from the bag, one at a time, and puts them in the order they were taken from the bag to create a sequence of colors. How many different sequences of colors are possible?
q-84983.worked_solution:
The number of permutations of $n$ objects taken $r$ at a time is given by the formula

$$
{}_{n}{P}_{r}=\frac{n!}{(n-r)!}.
$$

There are $9$ colored marbles, so $n=9.$ We want to select $4$ of those marbles to make a sequence of colors, so we have $r=4.$ 

Therefore, the number of different ways to choose the marbles is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{}_{9}{P}_{4} & =\frac{9!}{(9-4)!} \\  & =\frac{9!}{5!} \\  & =\frac{9\cdot 8\cdot 7\cdot 6\cdot \cancel{5!}}{\cancel{5!}} \\  & =9\cdot 8\cdot 7\cdot 6 \\  & =3\,024.\end{aligned}
$$

A bag contains 9 different colored marbles. Jamie takes 4 marbles from the bag, one at a time, and puts them in the order they were taken from the bag to create a sequence of colors. How many different sequences of colors are possible?

a
2016
b
3024
c
15120
d
120
e
1344
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The number of permutations of n objects taken r at a time is given by the formula nPr=n!(n−r)!.

There are 9 colored marbles, so n=9. We want to select 4 of those marbles to make a sequence of colors, so we have r=4.

Therefore, the number of different ways to choose the marbles is

q-84984.name: Question 3
q-84984.problem: A soccer coach must choose a defensive lineup for each of the $4$ defensive positions from a roster of $11$ defenders. How many potential starting defensive lineups are there?
q-84984.worked_solution:
The number of permutations of $n$ objects taken $r$ at a time is given by the formula

$$
{}_{n}{P}_{r}=\frac{n!}{(n-r)!}.
$$

There are $11$ defenders, so $n=11.$ We want to select $4$ of those defenders to play in each of the $4$ positions, so we have $r=4.$

Therefore, the number of different starting defensive lineups is

$$
\begin{aligned}{}_{11}{P}_{4} & =\frac{11!}{(11-4)!} \\  & =\frac{11!}{7!} \\  & =\frac{11\cdot 10\cdot 9\cdot 8\cdot \cancel{7!}}{\cancel{7!}} \\  & =11\cdot 10\cdot 9\cdot 8 \\  & =7\,920.\end{aligned}
$$
